newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean oil workers reiterate strike plan.
newsitem.headline: Chilean oil workers reiterate strike plan.

text.p: Chile's government has failed so far to persuade unions at state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (Enap) to accept plans to sell stakes in Enap's oil refineries to the private sector, union leaders said Thursday.
Union leaders and President Eduardo Frei's top political adviser, Juan Villarzu, met for talks to discuss the plans, after which unions reiterated their vow to protest any privatization with strikes.
They have set no firm date for a strike.

"We are not prepared to accept private capital in the way it has been explained to us. What we need is to strengthen the company in the state's own framework," said Hernan von Hausen, president of the National Federation of Oil Workers.
"We have reached no agreement, and the workers continue in our plan to carry out a national strategic strike if we don't get clear answers," he told reporters.

Union leaders from Enap, state metals smelting company Empresa Nacional de Mineria (Enami) and Codelco copper workers are expected to meet Monday to try to coordinate protest actions against the privatization plans, possibly including strikes.
President Eduardo Frei will announce plans to sell a controlling stake in Enap's two oil refineries, possibly as early as his annual speech to Congress on May 21, government sources have said.

The government declines to call the planned sale a privatization, calling it instead a "strategic association with the private sector." The sale is expected to affect only Enap's two refineries in Concon and Concepcion and not the rest of its business.
"We are not planning to privatize Enap. Such a proposal has never even crossed my desk," said Villarzu after meeting unions.

The refineries' workers will also be able to buy shares under the plan, similar to the way some shares were reserved for workers in the 1996 privatization of state copper company Codelco's Tocopilla power plant, sources said.
